newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTH AFRICAN UNION CONCERNED OVER RETIREMENT TAXES.
newsitem.headline: SOUTH AFRICAN UNION CONCERNED OVER RETIREMENT TAXES.

text.p: The 250,000-strong Federation of South African Labour Unions (Fedsal) on Monday expressed concern that government could raise tax on retirement fund rental income.

"Fedsal expressed concern that Government might in its next budget consider raising tax on retirement fund rental income from the current 17 percent to 30 percent originally proposed by the Katz Committee," Fedsal general secretary Dannhauser van der Merwe said in a statement.
He said the federation had met with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel and Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus in Pretoria on Monday to discuss its concerns.

"The Ministers assured Fedsal...that representatives of the different stakeholders would be given the opportunity to give inputs if a National Retirement Forum or similar meeting should be held in future to discuss any final...Committee proposals on retirement provision."
Fedsal had called the meeting due to uncertainties about "retirement nest eggs" which had led to many senior experienced employees retiring prematurely last year.

Van der Merwe said the organisation pointed out that deterring provision for one's own retirement by increasing the tax burden would be detrimental to the government "because less and less people will be encouraged to make adequate provision for themselves and will eventually rely on the State."
The organisation also requested that the government investigate the level of personal taxes which it believed was still too high.
